newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline leads oil complex losses at expiry.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline leads oil complex losses at expiry.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline futures led the oil complex mostly down at the close on Monday amid light volume and the expiry of the April refined products contracts.
With U.S. markets closed Friday for Easter, many players closed their positions on Thursday. London trade was also closed Monday for the holiday, taking out extra players.
"When you get the expiry spread out like this along with light volumes there are more dramatic movements," said a trader, referring to gasolines late-session fall.
April NYMEX gasoline future ended down 0.95 at 63.68 cents a gallon. Crude closed down 29 cents at $20.41 a barrel.
Traders said there was more interest in the May gasoline contract than the April one, particularly with the approach of the start of the driving season in late May.
Gasoline hit a day low of 63.00 cents after breaking support at 63.60 cents. The high for the day was 64.90 cents.
Gasoline knocked heating oil off its high of 57.50 cents.
April heat, the sole gainer of the day, ended up 0.65 cents at 56.72 cents a gallon, helped by cold weather in the Northeast and fund rolling out of April-May spread trades.
"It was pretty much a quiet day," said Tom Bentz, of ING Derivatives Clearing Inc.

Traders said news state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela's subsidiary Maraven plans to restart a downed fluid catalytic cracker at the giant Cardon refinery on Tuesday or Wednesday would likely add some bearish pressure on the market.
News of the refinery, which has a crude distillation capacity of 286,000 barrels per day, reached the market too late on Monday to be fully digested.
May crude, after trading range bound around unchanged levels all day, headed lower to its $20.41 a barrel settlement after breaking support at $20.50, traders said.
